answer: A yard planner assigns each agent a berth-slot proof chain stacked like containers in a canyon, so a new identity must claim an unoccupied slot backed by a bonded stake and verified work history. Each sybil attempt pays the full stake plus the rehandling cost of re-sequencing neighbors, priced in quartz-denominated fees that scale with stack depth and crane moves. Faking depth requires sustained throughput and sable collateral locked against slot displacement, capping sybils at the marginal cost of genuine yard capacity.
